```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)

# Read the dataset
file_path <- "customer_shopping_data.csv"
df <- read_csv(file_path)

# Create a copy to avoid modifying the original data
df_cleaned <- df

# Convert 'invoice_date' to datetime and extract month and hour
df_cleaned <- df_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    invoice_date = dmy(invoice_date),  # assumes day-first format
    OrderMonth = month(invoice_date),
    OrderHour = hour(invoice_date)
  )

# Calculate a simple "score" as quantity × price
df_cleaned <- df_cleaned %>%
  mutate(Score = quantity * price)

# Encode categorical features as numeric (factor levels)
df_cleaned <- df_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    gender_enc = as.numeric(as.factor(gender)) - 1,
    payment_method_enc = as.numeric(as.factor(payment_method)) - 1,
    category_enc = as.numeric(as.factor(category)) - 1,
    shopping_mall_enc = as.numeric(as.factor(shopping_mall)) - 1
  )

# Create user-level aggregated behavior features
user_stats <- df_cleaned %>%
  group_by(customer_id) %>%
  summarise(
    total_orders = n_distinct(invoice_no),
    avg_spent = mean(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_spent = sum(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    unique_categories = n_distinct(category)
  )

# Merge aggregated user features back into the main data frame
df_customer_shopping <- df_cleaned %>%
  left_join(user_stats, by = "customer_id")

# Keep only records where quantity and price are both greater than 0
df_customer_shopping <- df_customer_shopping %>%
  filter(quantity > 0, price > 0)

# Print the number of rows and count of missing values per column
cat("number of rows: ", nrow(df_customer_shopping), "\n")
print(colSums(is.na(df_customer_shopping)))

# Final cleaned dataset
df_customer_shopping

```

```{r}
# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(keras)
library(tensorflow)

# Read the CF scores and cleaned dataset
cf_scores <- read_csv("/Users/gongyueru/DS4420/cf_scores_for_mlp.csv")

# Clean df_ready: drop all .y columns and rename .x columns to clean names
df_ready_cleaned <- df_customer_shopping

# Merge CF scores
df_with_cf <- df_ready_cleaned %>%
  inner_join(cf_scores %>% select(customer_id, category, cf_score_scaled),
             by = c("customer_id", "category"))

# Define features and target
feature_columns <- c("age", "gender_enc", "payment_method_enc", "category_enc", "cf_score_scaled")
target_column <- "Score"

df_with_cf <- df_with_cf %>%
  mutate(log_score = log1p(Score))  # log(Score + 1)

# Extract features and target
X <- df_with_cf %>% select(all_of(feature_columns)) %>% as.matrix()
y <- df_with_cf$log_score

# Scale features
preproc <- preProcess(X, method = c("center", "scale"))
X_scaled <- predict(preproc, X)

# Train/test split
set.seed(42)
train_index <- createDataPartition(y, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
X_train <- X_scaled[train_index, ]
X_test <- X_scaled[-train_index, ]
y_train <- y[train_index]
y_test <- y[-train_index]

# Define MLP model
model <- keras_model_sequential() %>%
  layer_dense(units = 128, activation = "relu", input_shape = ncol(X_train)) %>%
  layer_dropout(rate = 0.4) %>%
  layer_dense(units = 64, activation = "relu") %>%
  layer_dense(units = 1)  # Output layer for regression

# Compile the model
model %>% compile(
  optimizer = "adam",
  loss = "mse"
)

# Train the model
history <- model %>% fit(
  x = X_train, y = y_train,
  validation_split = 0.2,
  epochs = 50,
  batch_size = 64,
  verbose = 1
)
```

```{r}
# Convert history to dataframe for plotting
plot_df <- as.data.frame(history$metrics)
plot_df$epoch <- 1:nrow(plot_df)

# Plot training vs validation loss
ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = epoch)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = loss, color = "Training Loss")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = val_loss, color = "Validation Loss")) +
  labs(title = "Training vs Validation Loss", y = "Loss (MSE)", x = "Epoch") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Training Loss" = "blue", "Validation Loss" = "red")) +
  theme_minimal()
```


```{r}
# transform log back to expm1
y_pred_log <- model %>% predict(X_test) %>% as.vector()
y_pred <- expm1(y_pred_log)  # inverse of log1p
y_true <- expm1(y_test)

# plot the true vs predict
ggplot(data.frame(True = y_true, Predicted = y_pred), aes(x = True, y = Predicted)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, color = "darkgreen") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Predicted vs Actual Scores", x = "Actual Score", y = "Predicted Score") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Predict and evaluate
y_pred <- model %>% predict(X_test) %>% as.vector()
rmse <- sqrt(mean((y_test - y_pred)^2))
mae <- mean(abs(y_test - y_pred))

cat(sprintf("RMSE: %.2f\n", rmse))
cat(sprintf("MAE: %.2f\n", mae))

```



```{r}
# get all the customer with all catergory of goods
all_user_category <- expand.grid(
  customer_id = unique(df_customer_shopping$customer_id),
  category = unique(df_customer_shopping$category)
)

# delete the category that user already buy
bought_pairs <- df_customer_shopping %>% select(customer_id, category)
candidates <- anti_join(all_user_category, bought_pairs, by = c("customer_id", "category"))

# get all the user's info from the original data
user_info <- df_customer_shopping %>%
  select(customer_id, age, gender_enc, payment_method_enc) %>%
  distinct()

# get all the category with the encode info from the data
category_info <- df_customer_shopping %>%
  select(category, category_enc) %>%
  distinct()

# join all the data into a new data be the recommended customer
candidates <- candidates %>%
  left_join(user_info, by = "customer_id") %>%
  left_join(category_info, by = "category") %>%
  left_join(cf_scores %>% select(customer_id, category, cf_score_scaled),
            by = c("customer_id", "category"))

# predict by using the data and scale the data
predict_X <- candidates %>%
  select(age, gender_enc, payment_method_enc, category_enc, cf_score_scaled) %>%
  as.matrix()

# transform log back to original data
predict_X_scaled <- predict(preproc, predict_X)

predicted_log_scores <- model %>% predict(predict_X_scaled) %>% as.vector()
candidates$predicted_score <- expm1(predicted_log_scores) 

# recommend 3 items for each user 
top_recommendations <- candidates %>%
  group_by(customer_id) %>%
  arrange(desc(predicted_score)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 3) %>%
  ungroup()

# print out the top 30 prediction
head(top_recommendations, 30)

```
